messages:
Samir (support): FYI escalated from Jane's team — their Private deployment in ap-southeast-1 is intermittently getting API connection hangs and TLS errors when talking to our eu-west-1 model endpoint. Errors: 502 / ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR / occasional 504 with 2–10s tail latency. Happens across app AZs, but not consistent.
Jane (customer): I can repro locally from their VPC when they hit the hostname api.redwood.prod.internal — about 1/10 requests fail, other times OK. Using our egress proxy.
Elaine (sre): Can you paste a minimal repro (curl + verbose) and a quick dig/nslookup from inside the customer's az/pod? We need to know if IP resolution differs.
Samir (support): Pasted from customer (anonymized):
```
# from app pod in ap-southeast-1
$ dig +short api.redwood.prod.internal
10.11.20.45
10.12.31.10

$ curl -v https://api.redwood.prod.internal/v1/ping
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood.prod.internal/v1/ping
*   Trying 10.11.20.45...
* Connected to api.redwood.prod.internal (10.11.20.45) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering http/1.1
* successfully set certificate verify locations:
  CAfile: /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
* SSL rehandshake not allowed
* error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number
```
Miguel (netops): Two A records returned — interesting. Could be one IP is fronting a different service or old proxy returning an unexpected TLS handshake. Do they have egress NAT/HTTP proxy that rewrites SNI or terminates TLS?
Jane (customer): They said egress proxy is passthrough tcp (no termination). NAT gateway + HA proxy in their VPC for outbound allowlist.
Yuna (eng-infra): Ask them to run `openssl s_client -connect 10.11.20.45:443 -servername api.redwood.prod.internal` and same to 10.12.31.10. If the cert CN/SAN differs, that's the problem (SNI mismatch -> cert for other host). Also check if any midbox is doing transparent TLS interception.
Samir (support): They ran openssl and returned:
```
# to 10.11.20.45
$ openssl s_client -connect 10.11.20.45:443 -servername api.redwood.prod.internal -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = Redwood, CN = Redwood Root CA
subject=CN = api.redwood.prod.internal
--- certificate chain ---
# OK, cert CN matches the hostname

# to 10.12.31.10
$ openssl s_client -connect 10.12.31.10:443 -servername api.redwood.prod.internal -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = OtherCorp, CN = edge-proxy.othercorp.net
subject=CN = edge-proxy.othercorp.net
--- certificate chain ---
# cert is for othercorp, so TLS host mismatch
```
Miguel (netops): That explains the ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR — one of the resolved IPs points at a third-party proxy/NAT that answers with a different cert. Why is that IP in resolution? Could be stale DNS in their VPC resolver or an anycast/ecmp path to a different region. What is the TTL on the record?
Samir (support): dig +trace shows the RR set at our side has TTL=60. Customer's VPC resolver returns both A records. They said their internal DNS caches are via dnsmasq on the egress host.
Yuna (eng-infra): Two possible root causes: 1) their egress path picks a different NAT IP that terminates TLS (misconfigured chain), or 2) DNS split view within their SP/network returns a wrong A for some AZs. We should ask them to: (a) temporarily force single IP `curl --resolve api.redwood.prod.internal:443:10.11.20.45 https://api.redwood.prod.internal/v1/ping` to confirm stability, (b) check which upstream resolver served the wrong record (`dig +short @<resolver>`), (c) check their egress proxy config for IP-based routing/transparent interception.
Jane (customer): Did the `--resolve` test — pinned to 10.11.20.45 — all pings succeeded, <10ms. Pin to 10.12.31.10 -> TLS cert mismatch as above.
Elaine (sre): That strongly points to an internal network path where some egress IP/peer routes reach an unrelated proxy. Action items for customer: flush dns cache on dnsmasq/egress host, ensure their egress NAT does not SNAT to third-party IPs, and remove any IP-based allowlisting that assumes our A records are stable. Also we should provide guidance: always allow by hostname + SNI and verify certs.
Miguel (netops): On our side, I'll verify our regional Anycast/egress pool health to ensure no accidental prefix collisions. Also check BGP announcements for the /24s that back our IPs.
Samir (support): Quick mitigation we gave: 1) ask customer to prefer our FQDN and avoid pinning/resolving to single IP long-term, 2) flush dns on egress (systemctl restart dnsmasq), 3) add egress allowlist for our IP ranges (but we warned them IPs can change; prefer hostname/SNI), 4) if they must pin IPs, use our published range and subscribe to IP change notifications.
Yuna (eng-infra): Long-term we should add a note in Private/VPC docs: "Do not rely on single A-record pinning; ensure egress proxies forward SNI and do not terminate TLS; flush DNS caches and keep TTLs low". I'll open a docs PR.
Samir (support): Customer did the dnsmasq restart and egress proxy tightened route table -> results: 24h without errors so far. They also adjusted monitoring to alert on cert CN mismatches.
Jane (customer): Thanks, that's been stable. Appreciate the quick help. :thumbsup:
RedwoodBot (bot): Incident note created #INC-2026-0427 referencing thread 1799991234.
Miguel (netops): Follow-up: we found a transient peer misannounce in one upstream region that briefly routed their egress address space through a partner that presented a generic proxy cert. Filed to infra.
Samir (support): Closing here for now; will reopen if recurrence. :white_check_mark:
